74180-stories-of-the-war-of-1812-and-the.title: Stories Of The War Of 1812 And The Mexican War
74180-stories-of-the-war-of-1812-and-the.creator: Unknown
74180-stories-of-the-war-of-1812-and-the.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. In June, 1812, the United States declared war against Great Britain. The chief cause of the war was the impressment of American seamen by the British. General Hull, with twenty-five hundred men, took post at Detroit, in Michigan. Soon afterward, the British general, Brock, with thirteen hundred men, appeared before Detroit, erected batteries, and summoned Hull to surrender. He refused, and the British opened their fire upon the works. On the 26th, they crossed the river and moved forward to the attack.

arxiv-1509-08842.title: Automatically Segmenting Oral History Transcripts
arxiv-1509-08842.creator: Ryan Shaw
arxiv-1509-08842.description: Abstract Dividing oral histories into topically coherent segments can make them more accessible online. People regularly make judgments about where coherent segments can be extracted from oral histories. But making these judgments can be taxing, so automated assistance is potentially attractive to speed the task of extracting segments from open-ended interviews.

arxiv-1512-03335.title: Adaptive multi-stage integrators for optimal energy conservation in molecular simulations
arxiv-1512-03335.creator: Mario Fernández-Pendás, Elena Akhmatskaya, J. M. Sanz-Serna
arxiv-1512-03335.description: Abstract We introduce a new Adaptive Integration Approach (AIA) to be used in a wide range of molecular simulations. Given a simulation problem and a step size, the method automatically chooses the optimal scheme out of an available family of numerical integrators. Although we focus on two-stage splitting integrators, the idea may be used with more general families.

arxiv-2304-13695.title: Efficient Approximation for Subgraph-Hitting Problems in Sparse Graphs and Geometric Intersection Graphs
arxiv-2304-13695.creator: Zdeněk Dvořák, Daniel Lokshtanov, Fahad Panolan, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue, Meirav Zehavi
arxiv-2304-13695.description: Abstract We investigate a fundamental vertex-deletion problem called (Induced) Subgraph Hitting : given a graph G G and a set ℱ \mathcal{F} of forbidden graphs, the goal is to compute a minimum-sized set S S of vertices of G G such that G − S G-S does not contain any graph in ℱ \mathcal{F} as an (induced) subgraph.

arxiv-2308-04479.title: Abundance of radioactive technetium in Przybylski’s star revisited
arxiv-2308-04479.creator: Sergei M. Andrievsky*, Sergey A. Korotin, Klaus Werner
arxiv-2308-04479.description: Abstract We have searched for lines of the radioactive element technetium (Tc) in the spectrum of Przybylski’s star (HD 101065). The nuclei of this chemical element are formed in the slow process of capturing thermalized neutrons. The possible lines of Tc I are heavily blended. We have synthesized the profile of one resonance line at 4297.

arxiv-2402-13272.title: Spontaneous Theory of Mind for Artificial Intelligence
arxiv-2402-13272.creator: Nikolos Gurney, David V. Pynadath, Volkan Ustun
arxiv-2402-13272.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nikolos Gurney, David V. Pynadath, Volkan Ustun. Existing approaches to Theory of Mind (ToM) in Artificial Intelligence (AI) overemphasize prompted, or cue-based, ToM, which may limit our collective ability to develop Artificial Social Intelligence (ASI). Drawing from research in computer science, cognitive science, and related disciplines, we contrast prompted ToM with what we call spontaneous ToM—reasoning about others’ mental states that is grounded in unintentional, possibly uncontrollable cognitive functions.

We shall define L 2 ​ [ a , b ] L^{2}[a,b] where the functions take bicomplex values. arxiv-2411-06317.description: Abstract I Introduction The internet has become a vital part of our everyday lives. With people relying on web application for getting their groceries, booking trips, scheduling doctor’s appointments, paying their taxes and more, a significant amount of sensitive, private user data flows through servers every second.

arxiv-2510-04553.title: Fast Witness Persistence for MRI Volumes via Hybrid Landmarking
arxiv-2510-04553.creator: Jorge Ruiz Williams
arxiv-2510-04553.description: Abstract We introduce a scalable witness-based persistent homology pipeline for full-brain MRI volumes that couples density-aware landmark selection with a GPU-ready witness filtration. Candidates are scored by a hybrid metric that balances geometric coverage against inverse kernel density, yielding landmark sets that shrink mean pairwise distances by 30–60% over random or density-only baselines while preserving topological features.

arxiv-2510-07596.creator: M. Van Cuyck, M. Béthermin, G. Lagache, A. Beelen
arxiv-2510-07596.description: Abstract Context. It is also essential to study these transitions to enhance component separation methods as LIM experiments improve in sensitivity. Aims.

arxiv-2510-17856.title: Carrier envelope phase and laser pulse shape effects on Schwinger vacuum pair production in super-Gaussian asymmetric electric fields
arxiv-2510-17856.creator: Abhinav Jangir, Anees Ahmed
arxiv-2510-17856.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Abhinav Jangir, Anees Ahmed. We investigate the combined effects of carrier envelope phase and laser pulse shape on electron-positron pair production in the presence of an external asymmetric super-Gaussian electric field by solving the quantum Vlasov equation. By varying the field asymmetry, the pulse shape from Gaussian to super-Gaussian, and the carrier envelope phase, we show the momentum distribution and the number density of created pairs to exhibit extreme sensitivity to these field characteristics.

arxiv-2512-21806.title: Optimal Robust Bounded Bias and Bounded Variance Designs Journal: U. Alberta preprint series
arxiv-2512-21806.creator: Douglas P. Wiens
arxiv-2512-21806.description: Abstract Designs which are minimax in the presence of model misspecifications have been constructed so as to minimize the maximum, over classes of alternate response models, of the integrated mean squared error of the predicted values. This mean squared error decomposes into a term arising solely from variation, and a bias term arising from the model errors.

arxiv-2601-21193.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Zecheng Zhao, Zhi Chen, Zi Huang, Shazia Sadiq, Tong Chen. Text-to-Video Retrieval (TVR) is an essential service in video platforms. In TVR, dense retrieval with dual-modality encoders leads in accuracy, but its computation and storage scale poorly with the corpus size. Thus, real-time and large-scale applications commonly adopt two-stage retrieval, where a fast recall model gathers a small pool of candidates, which are reranked by an advanced dense retriever.

arxiv-2602-17454.title: Privacy in Theory, Bugs in Practice: Grey-Box Auditing of Differential Privacy Libraries Volume: YYYY X DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX
arxiv-2602-17454.creator: Tudor Cebere, David Erb, Damien Desfontaines, Aurélien Bellet, Jack Fitzsimons
arxiv-2602-17454.description: Abstract . Differential privacy (DP) implementations are notoriously prone to errors, with subtle bugs frequently invalidating theoretical guarantees. Existing verification methods are often impractical: formal tools are too restrictive, while black-box statistical auditing is intractable for complex pipelines and fails to pinpoint the source of the bug.

pmc-10740859.title: Impact of CPAP Therapy on the Autonomic Nervous System
pmc-10740859.creator: Tea Friščić, Domagoj Vidović, Igor Alfirević, Edvard Galić
pmc-10740859.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a significant risk factor for cardiovascular disease (CVD) with increasing prevalence. An important mechanism of CVD development is a dysregulation of the autonomic nervous system (ANS). This prospective and controlled cohort study aimed to investigate ANS function in OSA including the response to long-term continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy by analyzing 24 h Holter electrocardiogram and 24 h Holter ambulatory blood pressure recording parameters. The study enrolled 57 patients who were newly diagnosed with severe OSA.

pmc-11327512.title: A deep learning approach to dysphagia-aspiration detecting algorithm through pre- and post-swallowing voice changes
pmc-11327512.creator: Jung-Min Kim, Min-Seop Kim, Sun-Young Choi, Kyogu Lee, Ju Seok Ryu
pmc-11327512.description: IntroductionThis study aimed to identify differences in voice characteristics and changes between patients with dysphagia-aspiration and healthy individuals using a deep learning model, with a focus on under-researched areas of pre- and post-swallowing voice changes in patients with dysphagia. We hypothesized that these variations may be due to weakened muscles and blocked airways in patients with dysphagia.

pmc-11404910.description: Breast cancer (BC) remains one of the most pervasive and complex malignancies. PANoptosis represents a recently identified cellular mechanism leading to programmed cell death. pmc-11662646.description: Clustered regularly-interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPRs) and CRISPR-associated (Cas) proteins protect bacteria and archaea from their viruses, and anti-CRISPRs (Acrs) are small virus-encoded proteins that inhibit CRISPR-Cas immunity. Over 80 families of Acrs have been described to date; however, only three of these subvert Type III CRISPR-Cas immunity.

pmc-12472167.title: Beyond Motor Decline in ALS: Patient-Centered Insights into Non-Motor Manifestations
pmc-12472167.creator: Anca Moțățăianu, Sebastian Andone, Smaranda Maier, Rareș Chinezu, Medeea Roman, Mihai Dumitreasă, Rodica Bălașa, Ioana Ormenișan, Cristian Falup-Pecurariu
pmc-12472167.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background and Objectives: Traditionally regarded as a purely motor disorder, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. However, it is increasingly recognized as a condition with a broader clinical spectrum, encompassing a variety of non-motor symptoms (NMS) that significantly impact patients’ quality of life and may influence disease progression and prognosis. Materials and Methods: The study included 44 patients diagnosed with probable or definite ALS and 35 healthy controls (HC).

pmc-12710922.title: HLA class-I genotyping to personalize Bacille Calmette–Guerin immunotherapy in bladder cancer
pmc-12710922.creator: Inmaculada Ruiz-Lorente, Lourdes Gimeno, Alicia López-Abad, Pedro López Cubillana, Tomás Fernández Aparicio, Lucas Jesús Asensio Egea, Juan Moreno Avilés, Gloria Doñate Iñiguez, Pablo Luis Guzmán Martínez-Valls, Gerardo Server, Belén Ferri, José Antonio Campillo, Francisco Galindo, María Victoria Ma
pmc-12710922.description: Bacille Calmette-Guerin (BCG) is the immunotherapy of choice for high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (BC), although recurrence eventually occurs in 50% of patients and 20% progress to advanced stages. This study evaluates the predictive value of human leukocyte antigen class-I (HLA-I) genotyping to guide BCG immunotherapy.

pmc-13122586.description: Physical unclonable functions (PUFs) based on nanophotonic materials offer a promising route toward secure and tamper-resistant authentication. uslaw-usc-t12-s1976.title: 12 U.S.C. § 1976 — Injunctive relief for persons against threatened loss or damages; equitable proceedings; preliminary injunctions
uslaw-usc-t12-s1976.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t12-s1976.description: United States Code, Title 12 (Banks And Banking); Chapter 22 (Tying Arrangements). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Any person may sue for and have injunctive relief, in any court of the United States having jurisdiction over the parties, against threatened loss or damage by reason of a violation of section 1972 of this title, under the same conditions and principles as injunctive.
